entry_conditions: Accept the demonstrated initial rest state or an in-distribution partial approach, handle pull, release/retreat, red approach or initial pickup within the full expanded slice. Inputs are two causal observations: qpos 0:9 and qvel 9:18, world TCP pose 18:25, red pose 25:32, blue pose 32:39, drawer d/vd 39:41 and goals 41:47; positions are metres, d is positive opening displacement, velocities retain recorded physical units, and quaternions are wxyz. Finger coordinates 7:9 are per-finger distances, not the command. At overlap entry around original index 195, measured d is about 0.1863 m, vd about 0.1071 m/s, fingers about 0.0071 m each and TCP z about 0.128 m. This is still a moving pull. Require reliable actual state/history for useful consequence estimates; the ensemble's uncertainty only attenuates candidate preference and is not an entry safety certificate. Failed grasps, jams and impacts are not represented by these entry examples.
exit_conditions: Useful exits include continued partial pulling for a successor that also knows late opening, release near d=0.300 m, rising retreat with opening preserved, red approach, or established initial red lift. d>0.26 m by itself does not establish relinquishment of the handle or red pickup. In observed release at index 240, fingers are about 0.03939 m each and command +1 while d remains near 0.300 m. By the supplied expanded post-action endpoint, d is about 0.300 m, red z about 0.142-0.143 m, fingers about 0.0182 m each and close command -1; red and TCP are close and moving together. These are support examples, not hard rejection/switching thresholds. Do not demand zero velocity, release of red, an extra retreat, or a sustained static hold. Skill exit guidance does not redefine the simultaneous three-goal whole-task completion contract.
overlap_role: This policy is trained over the entire start-0 expanded slice and shares original actions 195 through each assigned stop with evacuate_red, roughly 279-281 actions per demonstration. It learns late pull, handle release, upward retreat, reorientation/approach over red, descent, closure and initial lift as well as the preceding initial approach. The assigned prior predicts short action-conditioned successor outcomes across release and reattachment. Pull-time red/drawer coupling is softly deactivated as predicted fingers open and handle geometry is left; red/TCP coupling is used only in likely pickup geometry. It does not prescribe transporting red while retaining the handle or collapse every transition into a static state.
successor_readiness: Transfer actual most recent causal observation/history to evacuate_red, never a predicted endpoint as fact. Observe both d and vd; qvel and TCP change distinguish ongoing movement from waiting; total finger opening distinguishes the roughly 0.014 m handle grasp, 0.079-0.080 m released aperture and 0.0365 m red grasp. TCP/red distance and their two-observation relative motion distinguish approach from likely attachment. For demo1000 at 440, the TCP is within roughly 9 mm horizontally of red and 1 mm vertically but fingers are still open. At 450 fingers are closed around red but lift is not yet established; at 465 and 474 both red and TCP rise with nearly preserved offset. These observations support an inferred grasp rather than proving contact. The learned opening, release/retreat and lift readiness heads are action-conditioned advisory predictions, not a scripted switching predicate or oracle successor-success label.
failure_signatures: Observed opening that decreases unexpectedly during red approach; predicted and observed d/vd that disagree; continued over-pull after reaching the drawer's demonstrated limit; lateral travel while fingers still appear attached to the handle; a closing command without subsequent red/TCP co-motion; absent predicted or observed red lift; or predicted outcome preferences far from the learned demonstration anchor. Ensemble agreement alone cannot rule out any of these. Missing contact evidence and off-demonstration states are reasons for caution, not proof that this model can recover. The policy does not export a calibrated failure classifier.
continuation_guidance: The API chooses policy and invocation duration from actual observations, without a preset phase schedule. Continue this model for a local eight-action executed prefix when additional supported opening, release, retreat or red acquisition is desired; reobserve after execution. A successor takeover is already supported near d=0.186 m while increasing, not only after d>0.26. If choosing a later transfer, check that release/retreat or red acquisition is progressing and opening is preserved, rather than pausing until all motion stops. At the expanded initial-lift endpoint, transfer for red transport rather than relying on this model beyond its trained slice. The fixed interface ranks three learned paired epsilon/clean refinements inside denoising; it does not expose completed-chunk reranking, a variable-prefix planner or predicted readiness to the API as authoritative telemetry. Use actual history for the next decision.
limitations: Only successful local action neighborhoods and the measured expanded transitions support the model. Stage gates use geometry and finger opening rather than contact/force sensing. Counterfactual dynamics, common ensemble bias, clean-companion/epsilon mismatch, likelihood-proxy calibration and candidate collapse are unresolved. There is no IK, analytic kinematics, collision model, safe/unsafe discriminator, recovery controller, invariance guarantee or proof that opening and grasp will be preserved. Partial-transition support is measured training evidence, not a learned-policy success claim. No additional release, clearance, speed or hold condition is added to whole-task success.
